page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor based on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptographic instructions. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory, resulting in a compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, and it does not contain a dedicated GPU accelerator. Network capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear execution strengths alongside memory-bound tradeoffs. The instance achieves top-quartile results in single-core compute tasks, registering a stress-ng single-core score of 3075.37, a Geekbench single-core score of 1973.0, and strong text processing performance at 2483.0. Multi-threaded throughput aligns with the middle 50% of tested systems, shown by a stress-ng multi-core result of 6150.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 7535.23. In contrast, memory bandwidth metrics are comparatively modest, with uncached large-block read speeds measuring 36.57 GB/sec, placing in the bottom quartile. Application-level throughput reflecting memory and storage bottlenecks, such as Clang compilation, Redis SET operations at 5.5 million ops/sec, and static web serving, also rank in the lower quartile.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the ecs.c8a.xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute cycles for tasks that leverage dedicated core allocation without requiring extensive RAM footprints. Because the server lacks local NVMe disks and operates with an 8.0 GB memory envelope, it is unsuited for massive in-memory caching or high-IOPS transactional databases. The hardware profile is best aligned with dedicated background compute workers, batch parsing jobs, continuous integration agents, lightweight web microservices, and general CPU-bound processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, this instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Architectural benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, supported by AVX-512 instruction extensions. Multi-threaded integer and cryptographic throughput remain stable in the median range, whereas memory bandwidth and high-volume Redis operations place in the lower quartile. This configuration provides a cost-effective, dedicated compute environment for CPU-focused workloads that do not require heavy memory allocations, making it appropriate for background processing, lightweight microservices, and text-parsing pipelines.
